verdict.line: You lose if you facetank Infected Cleaver poke before level 3 and let him outscale your max-health growth; you win if you survive to 6 and use Cannibalism's lifesteal to outlast his Adrenaline Rush sustain in extended trades.

brief.thesis: This is a 49.6% even matchup over 113 games precisely because both kits are built to punish all-ins rather than win them — Mundo's Adrenaline Rush passive heals him back up, and your Cannibalism does the same for you. The one asymmetry: Infected Cleaver's damage scales off your current max health, so every point of Health you stack from Enrage kills or Heartsteel makes his free 4-second-cooldown poke hit harder on you specifically.

theirWindow.when: Q (Infected Cleaver) off cooldown, your W down
theirWindow.what: He can throw it from 975 range on a 4s cooldown for free poke scaled to your max health — don't stand still on cooldown or soak it with minions in the way.

yourWindow.what: Land Q (Cryptic Gaze) to stun him at 550 range, then use R (Cannibalism) at melee range to leech health to yourself while your empowered E (Enrage) autos chip his health down faster than Adrenaline Rush can regen it.

start.why: Measured at 53% win rate over 66 games and the clear majority pick — the regen and block passive directly answers Cleaver poke and his auto-attack harass.

boots.why: 58.8% win rate over 51 games, tied in pick rate with Swiftness — the flat physical reduction blunts both his Cleaver poke and his auto-attacks when he's using Masochism's AD spike.

core.why: Builds the max Health that fuels your Enrage passive and Cannibalism heal — this is the highest-sample build path at 42.9% win rate over 7 games.
Appears in every top build path on this patch and adds the damage-reduction shield that absorbs his sustained poke through a long lane.
Completes the measured 42.9% win rate path and punishes his auto-attack reliance directly.

the game goes long and you need mixed resistances to keep soaking damage
you want more wave-clear and all-in burst instead of pure durability

runes.keystoneWhy: Procs on him every 4 attacks in melee trades, converting your Health stacking into sustained lane healing against his own regen-based kit.

summoners.why: 84.3% pick rate at 52% win rate — Teleport lets you reset after losing the early poke exchange and still make wave-clear-focused waves count. Ghost+Teleport (40% pick, 40% win) is a reasonable alternative if you'd rather have sustained repositioning to dodge Cleaver than a flash escape.

playing.title: Hide from Cleaver before level 3
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this lane: before level 3 you have no stun to punish him, so use minions as cover against his 975-range Q and don't contest trades you can't win.

playing.title: Farm first, kill second
playing.detail: Both champions struggle to kill each other outright — prioritize wave management over forced all-ins until your item and level spikes line up.

playing.title: Stack HP carefully
playing.detail: Every point of max Health from Enrage kills or Heartsteel increases the raw damage Infected Cleaver deals to you — don't assume building tankier automatically makes his poke safer to ignore.

playing.title: Save Q for his all-in, not pokes
playing.detail: Cryptic Gaze stuns for a fixed duration on a cooldown that only drops to 8 seconds at rank 5 — hold it to lock him down during his own all-in rather than trading it for poke damage.

playing.title: Detonate W on your terms
playing.detail: Death's Caress's shield explodes automatically if it survives, but you can reactivate it to detonate early — pop it manually when he's in range rather than letting him kite the explosion.

playing.title: All-in only after level 6
playing.detail: Cannibalism's life-leech at melee range is your answer to Adrenaline Rush — before level 6 you have no sustain tool to outlast his regen in an extended fight.

playing.title: Respect his low-HP spike
playing.detail: Masochism gives him bonus Attack Damage scaled to missing Health, which is why he holds the solo-kill advantage in this matchup — don't chase him under 30% HP assuming he's safe to finish.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample-size figures above are measured from real games on the current patch (OP.GG); the mechanical reasoning — why each timing and trade pattern works — is my own tactical read, not measured data.
